headline: hl-cycles holds mild risk-on (since Oct 9) with BTC back at $81.9K, 0.5% above the $81.7K ETF cost basis, while stablecoin supply sits at z30 -3.16 ($305.3B vs mean30 $306.2B)
tldr: Regime is mild risk-on (66% BTC, 2 of 6 stress conditions on). Main change: BTC reclaimed the ETF cost basis ($81.7K) after the Oct 14 CPI-driven drop; hl-cycles' invalidation is a daily close below it. Main disagreement: price and funding are calm while the Compass Macro lens reads Restrictive (30) and stablecoin supply is contracting. Next catalyst: FOMC Oct 28, where a hike is a live possibility after the hot September CPI. Not financial advice.

domains.summary: FRED prints lag (newest Oct 15-16). 10Y 5.10% (Oct 15, from 5.24% on Oct 9), 2Y 4.77%, 2s10s +33bp (Oct 15 +33bp; Oct 16 +35bp), so the curve flattened as the 10Y fell faster than the 2Y. Fed funds effective 3.88% after a 25bp hike on Sep 16; September CPI printed 3.7% y/y headline, core 2.6% y/y (secondary source, unverified against BLS). Brent $126.55 (Oct 14) and WTI $101.91 (Oct 14) keep oil above the ~$100 inflation threshold; the Hormuz impasse is the cited driver. Dollar index last print 121.60 (Oct 9, stale). We read the stance as hawkish, liquidity tightening: stablecoin supply is falling and net liquidity was not available. A reversal in oil below $100 or a hold plus dovish FOMC language would change the read.

US cash market closed (Monday evening UTC); figures are last-session closes from Yahoo. SPY $766.60 (+0.44% 1d, -1.48% 5d), QQQ $718.36 (+1.21% 1d, -3.71% 5d), IWM $271.29 (-2.38% 5d): a one-day bounce inside a five-day slide, led by large-cap growth. VIX 18.28 on Yahoo (FRED 19.99 on Oct 16), up from 14.84 on Oct 9, so volatility has re-priced higher but stays below 20 on the latest print. Put/call and breadth were not collected; this is a VIX-only regime read. A VIX close above 25 or SPY below its Oct 16 low would change the read.

BTC $81,897 (+1.3% 24h), ETH $2,398 (+2.6%), SOL $104.18 (+3.4%), HYPE $77.92 (+2.1%): alts lead the bounce. HL total OI $10.93B (z30 -0.99), BTC OI $3.26B (z30 -1.62) lower than a day ago, so price rose while OI fell: short covering, a rally that may lack fresh demand. Funding sits at the 0.00125% hourly floor for BTC/ETH/SOL/HYPE (skew z30 +0.89, SOL z30 +1.32), so crowding is low. Fear & Greed 59 (z30 +0.73), BTC DVOL 37.5 (z30 -0.73), BTC dominance 59.64%. Stablecoin supply $305.3B is z30 -3.16, the one unusual reading: dry powder is shrinking. Crypto is moving on its own plus macro: Nasdaq fell 3.7% over 5 sessions while BTC is roughly flat, a modest divergence. A daily close below $81.7K (ETF cost basis) would change the read.

Last-session closes, individually: AAPL $342.94 (-0.15% 1d, +0.58% 5d), MSFT $533.52 (+0.84%, -1.41%), NVDA $217.09 (+1.38%, -4.08%), GOOGL $344.18 (+1.05%, -2.42%), AMZN $262.45 (+4.98%, +1.13%), META $705.44 (-0.55%, -5.05%). Dispersion is wide: AMZN and AAPL are holding while META and NVDA lead the 5-day losses. SMH $548.46 (+1.61% 1d, -7.20% 5d): semis weakness is concentrated and not yet repaired by the one-day bounce. AI-cycle headlines and earnings dates were not searched this run; the earnings calendar is a gap. A SMH close below $530 would extend the read.

The US-Israel-Iran conflict (since Feb 28) and the Strait of Hormuz impasse remain the main oil driver; the live search returned August-October trade coverage describing sanctions threats, a proposed Hormuz fee regime (Oman ~3%) and Brent up ~12% over two weeks. The search returned nothing dated Oct 19, so the freshest items are days to weeks old. Scheduled catalysts: FOMC decision Oct 28 (one source's claim of no October meeting conflicts with most calendars; verify on federalreserve.gov), NFP Nov 6, CPI Nov 10. A hot oil print keeps the inflation input live; a Hormuz reopening deal would be the main de-escalation path.

thesis.observe: BTC $81,897 (+1.3% 24h), 0.46% above the $81.7K ETF cost basis and 3.7% above the True Market Mean ($79.2K). hl-cycles: mild risk-on since Oct 9, allocation 66%, 2 of 6 stress conditions on, Compass 47 (Neutral, -3.7 over 30d), Macro lens 30. HL total OI $10.93B (z30 -0.99), BTC OI z30 -1.62, funding at the floor on BTC/ETH/SOL/HYPE. Stablecoin supply $305.3B (z30 -3.16). Fear & Greed 59. 10Y 5.10% (Oct 15), Brent $126.55 (Oct 14), VIX 18.28, September CPI 3.7% y/y headline.
thesis.infer: Price up with OI down and flat funding reads as short covering, not new leverage, so the bounce may lack fresh demand. Contracting stablecoin supply and a Restrictive Macro lens disagree with the risk-on regime label: the market is climbing without leverage against a tightening backdrop. Consensus is pricing a hold on Oct 28 with a hike later in the year; we read the hot CPI and oil above $100 as keeping a hike at the meeting live.
thesis.forecast: Base case (we lean here, low-confidence): BTC chops between the True Market Mean ($79.2K) and the ETF cost basis ($81.7K) into the Oct 28 FOMC; a daily close below $81.7K would end hl-cycles' risk-on leg, and a daily close above $105.6K with realized cap growing would confirm it. Tail case (low-confidence): a daily close below $79.2K could put the STH cost basis ($74.4K, about 9% below) in play. Second tail case (low-confidence): a hold with dovish language and oil below $100 may let stablecoin supply recover and BTC extend higher. Consensus is pricing a hold; we read the risk as skewing to a hawkish surprise.
thesis.disclaimer: Not financial advice. Market intelligence only — a reasoned read of public data, not a recommendation to buy or sell anything.
